# Save and restore object graphs

Saving only the values of individual objects cannot reconstruct two references to the same object or a cycle in which an object points to itself.
`RSKeyedArchiver` records each object once and saves reference IDs thereafter.
`RSKeyedUnarchiver` allocates each destination object and registers it in a reference map before filling its fields.
This note (08) traces both operations with a self-referential object.
See the [archiving guide](guide_10_Archiving.Rmd) for the public workflow and [note 02](tech_02_new_initialize.Rmd) for the separation of allocation and initialization.

## A cyclic graph for the example

The following `Node` has a string `value` and a `next_node` pointing to another `Node`.
Here, `next_node` points back to its owner, and the root R list contains that same `Node` twice.
`encodeWithCoder()` assigns keys to saved fields, and `initWithCoder()` reads them back.

```{r}
library(robjc)

Node <- RSObjectClass("Tech08Node",
  version = "1.0.0",
  protocols = list(RSCoding),
  public = list(
    value = NULL,
    next_node = NULL,
    initialize = function(value) {
      super$initialize()
      self$value <- value
      invisible(self)
    },
    encodeWithCoder = function(coder) {
      coder$encodeObjectForKey(self$value, "value")
      coder$encodeObjectForKey(self$next_node, "next")
      invisible(self)
    },
    initWithCoder = function(coder) {
      self$value <- coder$decodeObjectForKey("value")
      self$next_node <- coder$decodeObjectForKey("next")
      invisible(self)
    }
  )
)

source <- Node$new("hello")
source$next_node <- source
root <- list(source, source)
stopifnot(identical(root[[1L]], root[[2L]]))
stopifnot(identical(source$next_node, source))
```

## Three archive node types

`archive(root)` returns a record graph represented by an ordinary R list.
It contains the `root` node and `records` keyed by ID.
The three node types are `ref` for an RObjC object, `list` for traversing an ordinary R list, and `r` for a value left to R serialization.
RObjC instances, class generators, and protocol generators use `ref` nodes and matching records.

```{r}
archive <- RSKeyedArchiver$new()$archive(root)
stopifnot(identical(archive$format, "robjc-keyed-1"))
stopifnot(identical(archive$root$type, "list"))
stopifnot(identical(archive$root$values[[1L]]$type, "ref"))
stopifnot(identical(archive$root$values[[2L]]$type, "ref"))

id <- archive$root$values[[1L]]$id
stopifnot(identical(id, archive$root$values[[2L]]$id))
stopifnot(identical(archive$records[[id]]$fields[["next"]]$id, id))
stopifnot(identical(archive$records[[id]]$fields$value$type, "r"))
stopifnot(length(archive$records) == 1L)
```

This graph contains only one `Node`, so the same ID appears in both root entries and the `next` field.
The `value` string goes into an `r` node and is eventually serialized by R when the whole archive is saved, for example with `saveRDS()`.
robjc traverses ordinary R lists element by element but does not interpret reference structures inside arbitrary base R objects.

## Record an object before encoding its fields

When `RSKeyedArchiver` encounters an RObjC object, it uses the pointer string from `robjc_get_pointer()` as a reference ID.
For a new ID, it retains the source object in `.retained` and puts a record with `fields = NULL` in `.records` first.
It then calls the instance's `encodeWithCoder()` to fill the fields.
On encountering the same ID again, it returns only a `ref` node instead of repeating `encodeWithCoder()`.

```text
First encounter with Node
  → create ID, retain Node, register incomplete record
  → follow value and next in encodeWithCoder()
  → next has the registered ID, so return only a ref
  → complete the record's fields
```

Registering the record before following fields prevents infinite recursion on self-reference.
`.retained` keeps source objects alive during archiving so that garbage collection cannot free one and let its pointer ID be reused for another object.
The retention map is released when archiving finishes.
During decoding, saved IDs are opaque strings, not pointers to restored objects.

## Resolve classes before restoration

Each record contains a `kind`, class name, saved version, and, if registered, a package and class ID.
Built-in and registered package classes can be resolved automatically; a generator can be supplied for a class defined in a script.
`RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(archive)` loads the data without restoring objects yet.
Inspect candidate mappings with `showAllClasses()`, supply a tibble or `RSMutableDictionary` to `setClasses()` if needed, and then call `decode()`.

```{r}
decoder <- RSKeyedUnarchiver$new(unserialize(serialize(archive, NULL)))
mapping <- decoder$showAllClasses(remove_default = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(mapping$class_name, "Tech08Node"))
stopifnot(is.null(mapping$decoder_class[[1L]]))

mapping$decoder_class[1L] <- list(Node)
decoder$setClasses(mapping)
stopifnot(identical(decoder$showAllClasses(remove_default = FALSE)$decoder_name,
                    "Tech08Node"))
```

Before restoring the root, `decode()` checks for unresolved classes and required `initWithCoder()` methods.
Within `initWithCoder()`, `savedClassVersion()` provides the saved version for migration from an older format.
Class mapping is separate from the archive format, so a saved name can be explicitly mapped to a different current generator.

## Register the destination before decoding its fields

The decoder's `.object_map` maps saved IDs to destination objects.
On reading a `ref`, it first checks whether the ID is already in that map.
For a new ID, it finds the destination generator and normally allocates an instance with `robjc_allocate()`, without calling `initialize()`.
It registers that instance in `.object_map`, makes the record fields available, and only then runs `initWithCoder()`.

```text
Decode the first ref(id)
  → allocate an empty Node instance
  → register it in .object_map[id]
  → read value and next in initWithCoder()
  → the next ref(id) returns the same .object_map[id] instance
  → finish the original Node
```

Reversing registration and `initWithCoder()` would start restoring the same ID again when `next` is read.
Early registration permits references to an object whose fields are still incomplete, preserving both cycles and shared references.

```{r}
restored <- decoder$decode()
stopifnot(identical(restored[[1L]], restored[[2L]]))
stopifnot(identical(restored[[1L]]$next_node, restored[[1L]]))
stopifnot(identical(restored[[1L]]$value, "hello"))
stopifnot(!identical(restored[[1L]], source))
```

Records that refer to class or protocol generators put the destination generator in the reference map and return it.
They do not call `initWithCoder()` as instances do.
For a Singleton, the default `robjc_allocate()` returns the existing shared instance, so decoding does not make a separate ordinary instance.

This order separates the shape of the saved graph from how current classes interpret their fields.
`initWithCoder()` remains responsible for validating those fields and completing the object's state.
